title: Kollar injectivity for a smooth divisor in a power of a line bundle
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-scheme of pure dimension $n\geq0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $\omega_Y=\bigwedge^n\Omega^1_{Y/F}$, where the sheaf of Kähler differentials is obtained by gluing $\Omega_{B/F}$ on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and the exterior power is the quotient of the $n$th tensor power by the alternating multilinearity relations, with $\bigwedge^0\Omega^1_{Y/F}=\mathcal O_Y$. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $m\geq2$ be an integer, and let $0\ne s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes m})$. Assume its zero scheme $D=Z(s)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] is smooth over $F$; the empty zero scheme is allowed. Then for every $j\geq0$ the homomorphism
$$H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\;H^j(\cdot s)\;}H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes L^{\otimes(m+1)})$$
is injective. Here $\cdot s$ is the sheaf morphism locally given by multiplication by the function representing $s$, $H^j=R^j\Gamma$ is Zariski module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], and tensor products and nonnegative tensor powers are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No ampleness hypothesis on $L$ is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally: Mihnea Popa, Kodaira dimension of algebraic varieties, section 1.6 opening paragraph (printed p.22: extension to algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields), Theorem 1.6.6 and proof (printed pp.26--27), with m>=2; author notes read online at https://people.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/271/Kodaira-posted.pdf. This is the injectivity input, not Theorem 1.6.1 itself.

proof.text: If $D=\varnothing$, every local function representing $s$ is a unit: its principal ideal defines the empty closed subscheme. Thus multiplication by $s$ is a sheaf isomorphism, whose inverse induces an inverse in cohomology. Assume henceforth $D\ne\varnothing$. On an integral scheme the local functions representing a nonzero section of a line bundle are nonzero: if one were zero on a nonempty open, injectivity into the common function field would make all representatives zero, contradicting $s\ne0$. They are therefore nonzerodivisors. The image of $s:L^{-m}\to\mathcal O_Y$ is exactly the ideal of $D$ by the definition of $Z(s)$; this identifies that ideal with $L^{-m}$.

source.place: Theorem 1.6.6, setup; elementary empty-divisor case and regularity of the section written out.

proof.text: Apply the cyclic-cover lemma to the given $(Y,L,m,s)$. It supplies a smooth projective root cover $W$, without assuming it connected, and the cohomology character decompositions compatible with $d$. Apply the first-Hodge-differential lemma to $W$ over $F$. The whole map $H^q(W,d)$ is zero for every $q\geq0$. Its character-one block is the map $H^q(Y,\nabla_1)$, so that map is zero. This uses sheaves of $F$-vector spaces for the differential, not an assertion of $\mathcal O$-linearity.

source.place: WANTED locally; Proposition 1.6.5 and proof of Theorem 1.6.6, pp.26--27.

proof.text: Put $N=L^{-1}$ and let $r:N\to N\otimes\mathcal O_D$ be restriction, viewed on $Y$. The cyclic-cover lemma gives $\nabla_1(b e^{-1})=(db+(b/m)du/u)\otimes e^{-1}$ and the residue map kills $db$ and sends $du/u$ to $1$. Hence $r=m(\operatorname{res}_D\otimes1)\nabla_1$ on every trivializing open and therefore globally. Applying $F$-linear sheaf cohomology and step 2 gives $H^q(Y,r)=0$ for every $q\geq0$. The factor $m$ (not $1/m$) multiplies the residue composite; division by $m$ is legitimate because $\operatorname{char}F=0$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Lemma 1.6.7, p.27, with its residue coefficient explicitly computed.

proof.text: Step 1 gives the short exact sequence $0\to L^{-(m+1)}\xrightarrow{\cdot s}L^{-1}\xrightarrow{r}L^{-1}\otimes\mathcal O_D\to0$: on a trivializing open it is $0\to A\xrightarrow{\cdot u}A\to A/(u)\to0$, with $u$ a nonzerodivisor. Apply the cited long exact derived-functor sequence for global sections. Exactness at $H^q(Y,L^{-1})$, together with $H^q(Y,r)=0$, says that $H^q(Y,\cdot s):H^q(Y,L^{-(m+1)})\to H^q(Y,L^{-1})$ is surjective for all $q\geq0$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Theorem 1.6.6 proof, p.27, short exact sequence and its long exact cohomology sequence.

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq n$ set $q=n-j$ and apply functorial Serre duality to $v=\cdot s:L^{-(m+1)}\to L^{-1}$. Its dual sheaf map is multiplication by the same local function $u$, so $\operatorname{id}_{\omega_Y}\otimes v^\vee$ is exactly the map $\omega_Y\otimes L\to\omega_Y\otimes L^{m+1}$ in the item. Under the duality isomorphisms its degree-$j$ cohomology map is precomposition with the surjection of step 4. Such precomposition is injective: if a functional vanishes on the image of a surjective map, it vanishes everywhere. For $j>n$ the source is zero by the vanishing clause of the same duality lemma. This proves every asserted degree.
